"""Moving-average window selection by honest (no-lookahead) cross-validation.

Evaluates MA windows {3, 7, 14, 28} by walk-forward one-step-ahead MAE over
days 60-399. The day-t forecast for window w is mean(sales[t-w:t]) -- it uses
ONLY days strictly before t. Because the series has a regime change at day
200 (mean 80 -> 120), short windows should win.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from gen import generate, CHANGE_DAY

WINDOWS = [3, 7, 14, 28]
EVAL_START = 60
EVAL_END = 399  # inclusive
ROLL_WINDOW = 30


def one_step_forecasts(sales, w):
    """One-step-ahead MA(w) forecasts.

    fc[t] = mean(sales[t-w:t]) for t >= w, NaN otherwise.
    Strictly causal: uses only days < t.
    """
    s = np.asarray(sales, dtype=float)
    fc = np.full(len(s), np.nan)
    for t in range(w, len(s)):
        fc[t] = s[t - w:t].mean()
    return fc


def walk_forward_mae(sales, w, eval_start=EVAL_START, eval_end=EVAL_END):
    """Mean absolute one-step error over days eval_start..eval_end inclusive."""
    s = np.asarray(sales, dtype=float)
    fc = one_step_forecasts(sales, w)
    err = np.abs(fc[eval_start:eval_end + 1] - s[eval_start:eval_end + 1])
    return float(err.mean())


def rolling_mae(sales, w, roll_window=ROLL_WINDOW,
                eval_start=EVAL_START, eval_end=EVAL_END):
    """Rolling `roll_window`-day MAE of absolute one-step errors.

    Returned as a pandas Series indexed by day, restricted to the evaluation
    range (first valid value at day eval_start + roll_window - 1).
    """
    s = np.asarray(sales, dtype=float)
    fc = one_step_forecasts(sales, w)
    err = pd.Series(np.abs(fc - s), index=np.arange(len(s)))
    r = err.rolling(roll_window).mean()
    return r.loc[eval_start + roll_window - 1:eval_end]


def select_window(sales, windows=WINDOWS):
    """Return (best_window, {window: mae})."""
    maes = {w: walk_forward_mae(sales, w) for w in windows}
    best = min(maes, key=lambda w: maes[w])
    return best, maes


def summary_table(sales=None, windows=WINDOWS):
    """Build and print the summary table; return it as a string too."""
    if sales is None:
        sales = generate()["sales"].to_numpy()
    sales = np.asarray(sales, dtype=float)

    best, maes = select_window(sales, windows)
    lo, hi = CHANGE_DAY, CHANGE_DAY + 40  # days 200-240 inclusive

    lines = []
    lines.append("Moving-average window selection (walk-forward, no lookahead)")
    lines.append(f"data: 400 days, regime change at day {CHANGE_DAY} "
                 f"(mean 80 -> 120), eval days {EVAL_START}-{EVAL_END}")
    lines.append("")
    header = f"{'window':>6} | {'overall MAE':>11} | {'max roll-30 MAE d200-240':>25}"
    lines.append(header)
    lines.append("-" * len(header))
    rows = []
    for w in windows:
        rm = rolling_mae(sales, w)
        seg = rm.loc[lo:min(hi, rm.index.max())]
        max_roll = float(seg.max())
        row = f"{w:>6} | {maes[w]:>11.3f} | {max_roll:>25.3f}"
        marker = "  <-- selected" if w == best else ""
        lines.append(row + marker)
        rows.append((w, maes[w], max_roll))
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"selected window: {best}")

    table = "\n".join(lines)
    print(table)

    # Sanity assertions on honest-CV behavior under the regime change.
    assert best <= 7, (
        f"expected a short window (<=7) to win after regime change, got {best}")
    roll_by_w = {}
    for w in windows:
        roll_by_w[w] = rolling_mae(sales, w)
    seg28 = roll_by_w[28].loc[lo:min(hi, roll_by_w[28].index.max())]
    seg3 = roll_by_w[3].loc[lo:min(hi, roll_by_w[3].index.max())]
    assert (seg28 > 25).any(), (
        "window-28 rolling 30-day MAE should spike above 25 in days 200-240")
    assert (seg3 < 18).all(), (
        "window-3 rolling 30-day MAE should stay under 18 in days 200-240")

    return table


if __name__ == "__main__":
    df = generate()
    summary_table(df["sales"].to_numpy())

        f"with MAEs {maes}"

    roll28 = rolling_mae(sales, 28)
    roll3 = rolling_mae(sales, 3)

    seg3 = roll3.loc[lo:min(hi, roll3.index.max())]

    assert (seg28 > 25).any(), (
        f"window-28 rolling MAE should exceed 25 in days {lo}-{hi}; "
        f"max was {seg28.max():.2f}"
    )
    assert (seg3 < 18).all(), (
        f"window-3 rolling MAE should stay under 18 in days {lo}-{hi}; "
        f"max was {seg3.max():.2f}"
    )


def test_no_lookahead_future_reversal_changes_nothing(sales):
    """Day-t forecasts must use only days < t.

    Reverse the future segment (days >= T) and verify every forecast up to
    and including day T is bit-for-bit unchanged.
    """
    for w in WINDOWS:
        base = one_step_forecasts(sales, w)
        for t in (150, CHANGE_DAY + 5):
            perturbed = sales.copy()
            perturbed[t:] = perturbed[t:][::-1]
            after = one_step_forecasts(perturbed, w)

            # forecast at day t itself only uses days < t, so it too must match
            unchanged = np.isnan(base[:t + 1]) & np.isnan(after[:t + 1])
            same = base[:t + 1] == after[:t + 1]
            assert np.all(unchanged | same), (
                f"lookahead detected: window-{w} forecasts at days <= {t} "
                f"changed when the future segment was reversed"
            )
            # ...but at least some later forecast must differ (perturbation effective)
            later = ~(
                (np.isnan(base[t + ROLL_WINDOW:]) & np.isnan(after[t + ROLL_WINDOW:]))
                | (base[t + ROLL_WINDOW:] == after[t + ROLL_WINDOW:])
            )
            assert later.any(), (
                f"perturbation had no effect for window {w}; test is vacuous"
            )

    """Cross-check MAE against a naive loop implementation."""
    w = 7
    s = sales
    fc = one_step_forecasts(s, w)
    errs = [abs(fc[t] - s[t]) for t in range(EVAL_START, len(s))]
    assert walk_forward_mae(s, w) == pytest.approx(np.mean(errs))
